note: Vietnamese street food, home cooking, regional specialities, festival food and the chains Vietnamese people actually eat at, written for a catalogue that began Malaysian and is becoming Asian. WEB SEARCH WAS UNAVAILABLE FOR THIS ROUND: every figure here is a model estimate reasoned from the dish's own ingredients and anchored against comparable rows already in the catalogue (the pan-Asian round's nine Vietnamese dishes, the Malaysian noodle-soup and rice-plate rows, the MyFCD component rows, the Thai and Philippine rounds). Nothing was read off a published table, so every row is verified:false and source:model_estimate. The Vietnamese dishes the catalogue already holds — Pho Bo, Pho Ga, Bun Bo Hue, Bun Thit Nuong, Bun Cha Hanoi, Banh Mi, Banh Mi Ga, Goi Cuon, Banh Xeo, Com Tam Suon Nuong, Ca Phe Sua Da — are deliberately absent, and where a regional variant is genuinely a different bowl it carries the region in its name. Portions are the Vietnamese street portion: a noodle bowl is the standard tô, a com tam is one plate, a banh mi is one 20 cm baguette, and a ca phe phin is the small glass it is actually poured into.
